title: Targeted RNA of NSCLC patient number 17
source_name: formalin-fixed paraffin embedded biopsies or archival surgically resected specimens collected prior to treatment initiation
extract_protocol: [sample preparation]  10mm2 of 5 micrometer FFPE tumour macrodissection tissue were lysed using HTG Lysis Buffer, followed by proteinase K digestion, and then transferred to an HTG EdgeSeq platform according to manufacturer protocols (HTG Molecular Diagnostics, Inc., Tucson, AZ). | The Oncology Biomarker Panel was used to  capture RNA expression levels of gene targets  on the HTG EdgeSeq platform according to manufacturer protocols (HTG Molecular Diagnostics, Inc., Tucson, AZ). The resulting DNA probes were quantitatively amplified with polymerase chain reaction adding extended primers ,including sequencing primer and sample barcode sequences. | Library samples were cleaned up to remove excess primers, quantitated, pooled and sequenced using Illumina NextSeq500 sequencer using 50-cycles single end ((Illumina, Inc.). | Targeted RNASeq
data_processing: Illumina bcl2fastq is used for generation of FASTQ files | HTG EdgeSeq Parser software (version 5.1) is used for alignment to a priori defined target sequences.  Requirements include %Q30 >= 85%, %PF >= 75%, and 180 < CD < 290 | Post-sequencing quality control using three quality control metrics: 1) Percent of reads allocated to the Positive control probe must not exceed 15%, 2) Total aligned reads must exceed 1,500,000, and 3) Relative Standard Deviaion (CV) of counts within a sample must exceed 0.1 (CV is calculated after removal of counts from ANT and POS control probes and log2 transformation after addition of 2 to avoid taking the log of 0). A log2 CPM normalization is then processed. | Supplementary_files_format_and_content: Nivobio_log2cpm_data.csv

extract_protocol: [sample preparation]  10mm2 of 5 micrometer FFPE tumour macrodissection tissue were lysed using HTG Lysis Buffer, followed by proteinase K digestion, and then transferred to an HTG EdgeSeq platform according to manufacturer protocols (HTG Molecular Diagnostics, Inc., Tucson, AZ). | The Oncology Biomarker Panel was used to  capture RNA expression levels of gene targets  on the HTG EdgeSeq platform according to manufacturer protocols (HTG Molecular Diagnostics, Inc., Tucson, AZ). The resulting DNA probes were quantitatively amplified with polymerase chain reaction adding extended primers ,including sequencing primer and sample barcode sequences. | Library samples were cleaned up to remove excess primers, quantitated, pooled and sequenced using Illumina NextSeq500 sequencer using 50-cycles single end ((Illumina, Inc.). | Targeted RNASeq
data_processing: Illumina bcl2fastq is used for generation of FASTQ files | HTG EdgeSeq Parser software (version 5.1) is used for alignment to a priori defined target sequences.  Requirements include %Q30 >= 85%, %PF >= 75%, and 180 < CD < 290 | Post-sequencing quality control using three quality control metrics: 1) Percent of reads allocated to the Positive control probe must not exceed 15%, 2) Total aligned reads must exceed 1,500,000, and 3) Relative Standard Deviaion (CV) of counts within a sample must exceed 0.1 (CV is calculated after removal of counts from ANT and POS control probes and log2 transformation after addition of 2 to avoid taking the log of 0). A log2 CPM normalization is then processed. | Supplementary_files_format_and_content: Nivobio_log2cpm_data.csv
